phases.title: Review and approve
phases.intro: Everything still waiting on your eyes or your decision. Approve each one, or send feedback. When agents change something in response, it comes back here as a new version, with your feedback shown beside it. **When every item is approved, the code freeze begins.**

phases.title: Before launch: accounts, keys and settings
phases.intro:
Work through these in any order. Each value you collect is saved here and goes into the env files at the end of this phase. Steps marked *Waits on agents* need a piece of code first; the note says which.

**One rule protects the live site.** Production keeps the keys it has now. New, separate keys go to staging, and development gets fakes. If you ever do replace a production key, the order is: push it to Netlify, ask Claude to redeploy the live site, check it works, and only then revoke the old one. All of that must finish before launch day.

phases.title: Launch day
phases.intro: In order, top to bottom. Start only after the code freeze and once every *Before launch* step is done. Allow about three hours, on a weekday morning.

phases.title: After launch
phases.intro: The checks over the following days, and the dates to remember.

sections.title: Look at staging
sections.intro: Use your iPhone where it says so. Staging is the current build: https://staging--north-foster-farm.netlify.app/

sections.title: Decisions
sections.intro: Each has a recommendation. Approving accepts the recommendation; to decide otherwise, write your answer and press **Send feedback**.

steps.title: Make a folder for this launch in your password manager
steps.body:
Create a folder (or vault) named **NFF launch**. Whenever this guide says to save something to your password manager, it goes there. Values you paste into this guide are also saved in this browser, so you can stop and come back later.

The guide has two exports at the top. **Export report for Claude** is safe to paste into the chat. **Export secrets** is a full backup of everything, including secrets. Save it as a secure note in the NFF launch folder, and never paste it anywhere else.

steps.title: Check which Netlify plan the team is on
steps.body:
Open Usage & billing, then Billing details. Note whether it says **Starter** (the older plans) or a **credit-based** plan (Free, Personal or Pro).

This matters on the credit-based Free plan: a production deploy costs 15 of 300 monthly credits, and when credits run out, every site on the team is paused. Write the plan name below so Claude can check the launch fits.

steps.title: Bring in production's current values
steps.body:
Your current `.env` in the project folder is a production file: it holds the keys the live site uses. Open it in your editor, select everything, copy, and paste it into the box below. The guide reads each line and fills in the matching production fields further down: Square, PayPal, Resend, Axiom and Healthchecks. The pasted text itself isn't kept, only the values it fills in, and it never leaves this browser.

Afterwards, open the steps below; each production field should already be filled. Anything still empty is a value your `.env` didn't have, and the step says where to get it.

steps.title: Turn on two-factor sign-in everywhere
steps.body:
Every account that can reach a secret needs two-factor sign-in, with its recovery codes saved in the **NFF launch** folder of your password manager. Check each, and turn it on where it is off: **Netlify, GitHub, Square, PayPal, Resend, Cloudflare, Axiom, Healthchecks, UptimeRobot, Fastmail.** Any second factor works; an authenticator app or a security key is better than a text message.

Tick this when all ten are done. Claude cannot see any of them.

steps.title: Check why production's Square webhook has never succeeded
steps.body:
Production's health check shows no Square webhook delivery ever accepted. Either Square sends nothing, or every delivery fails the signature check. Find out which:
1. Open the Developer Console and open your production app.
2. In the left pane choose **Webhooks**, then **Logs**. At the top, choose **Production**.
3. Look at the **Status code** column. That's what *our* server answered, not Square. **401** means the signature check rejected it; nothing listed means nothing was sent.
4. Then open **Webhooks → Subscriptions** (Production). Check the notification URL is exactly `https://www.northfosterfarm.com/api/square/webhook`. The signature covers the URL character for character, so the bare domain, a trailing slash or `http` all break it.

Write what you found in the note on this step.

- **Locations:** North Foster Farm's location ID, `L6PRYPQ7VW659`. Every sale lives there now (#267), not at the northfosterfarm.com location; step sq-location moves the site.
- **Webhooks → Subscriptions:** open the production subscription, then **Show** the Signature Key.

If you fixed the subscription URL in the previous step, its signature key is unchanged.

**Note, 2026-10-24:** For the release a new Square application is created (#331, a line in #237) and its token, application id and webhook replace production's values. Check the new app's values, not the old ones, and revoke the old app's token after the test order passes.

steps.title: Launch blocker: move the site to North Foster Farm's location
steps.body:
You decided every sale and all stock live at one Square location, **North Foster Farm** (`L6PRYPQ7VW659`), on #267. The site reads its stock there and takes its orders there once these are done. The full answer, with every place the code uses the location, is on #267.
1. **Token:** in the Developer Console, open the production app. Under **OAuth**, or wherever the access token's permissions are set, make sure it includes `INVENTORY_READ`. Without it the site never sees Square's counts and sells by its own instead, silently. A personal access token already has every permission.
2. **Tracking:** in the Square Dashboard, under **Items**, turn on stock tracking at North Foster Farm for every item you count. It is off on all three Tenders, Sweet Italian Sausage and Feet. Cornish hens and ground chicken are archived and can stay off.
3. **Before tracking items come back:** Medium and Small eggs are not offered at any location. Add them at North Foster Farm before either goes back on sale, or Square refuses the website's orders for them. When Feet return, clear their **Sold out** mark at North Foster Farm.
4. **Counts:** enter tonight's physical counts at North Foster Farm, or tell Claude to load them.
5. **The switch, at a quiet hour:** set `SQUARE_LOCATION_ID` to `L6PRYPQ7VW659` in `.env.production`, push the env and redeploy. Then run `bin/nff env verify --production`; its Square line must say ok.
6. **Proof:** in the Dashboard, set Backs 1.0 - 1.9 lbs to 2 at North Foster Farm. The order page says "2 left" on its next load. Set it back afterward.

Orders placed at the old location before the switch still update and refund where they were placed. Staging runs on the sandbox and is untouched.

steps.title: Launch blocker: ring up one item at zero stock
steps.body:
This proves a sale on the phone still goes through when the count is 0 or below. A warning is fine; a block is not.
1. In the Square Dashboard, turn on tracking for **Backs 1.0 - 1.9 lbs** at North Foster Farm and set its count there to **0**.
2. On your iPhone, in Square POS, go to **Settings**, then **Location**, and choose **North Foster Farm**.
3. Ring up 1 Backs and take it as cash. **Pass:** the sale completes.
4. In the Dashboard, Backs at North Foster Farm reads **-1**, and no other location changed.
5. Ring up one more. It still completes, and the count reads **-2**.
6. Refund both sales on the phone, choosing to return the items to stock. The count goes back to **0**.

If step 3 blocks the sale, look in the Dashboard's inventory settings for the one that stops sales at zero stock, and write what you find in the note on this step.

steps.title: Make a separate Square app for staging
steps.body:
Staging gets its own application, so nothing is shared with production or development.
1. In the Developer Console, on Applications, create a new application named **NFF Staging**.
2. Set the toggle to **Sandbox**. On **Credentials**, copy the **Sandbox application ID** and **Show** the **Sandbox Access token**.
3. On **Locations** (Sandbox), copy the location ID.
4. **Webhooks → Subscriptions → Sandbox → Add subscription.** Name it "staging", with the URL below. Choose the newest API version and tick `payment.created`, `payment.updated`, `refund.created`, `refund.updated` and `order.updated`. Save, open it, and **Show** the Signature Key.
5. Optional: **Apple Pay → Add Sandbox Domain** for `staging--north-foster-farm.netlify.app`, if you want to try Apple Pay on staging (Safari only).

Note: every app under one Square login shares the same sandbox data. That's why development gets its own login in the next step.

steps.title: Add the live webhook (P2)
steps.body:
Still on the live app, scroll to **Live Webhooks** and choose **Add Webhook**. Paste the URL below, tick the events below, and save. The webhook appears in the list with an **ID**; copy it. PayPal never sends this ID in its messages, so this is the only place to get it.

Without this webhook, the site never hears about Venmo captures or refunds made in PayPal. Adding it before launch is harmless.

**Do this before the release.** Subscribe it to exactly those two events. Then set the ID on Netlify's production context as `PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID` (it is not a secret), deploy (a change to Netlify's environment applies only to a new deploy; see `docs/secrets.md`) and confirm it with `bin/nff env verify --production`. The live Venmo check cannot pass without it: the webhook is what finishes a Venmo payment when the browser is closed.

steps.title: Check the Resend keys and webhook the send breaker needs
steps.body:
The send breaker (a launch blocker) stops all email and deletes the sending key if mail goes out that our code did not send, or too much of it. It needs three things in Resend.
1. **API Keys:** `RESEND_AUDIENCE_KEY` shows **Full access**. The breaker deletes the sending key with it, so this gates the rehearsal below.
2. **Webhooks:** the `/api/resend/webhook` endpoint has `email.sent`, `email.bounced` and `email.complained` ticked.
3. **The sending key's name:** Resend's key list cannot say which key is which, so the breaker finds it by name. Type the sending key's name below; it goes into `RESEND_SENDING_KEY_NAME` in `.env.production`.

Done when, after the env push and deploy, `bin/nff breaker status --production` prints "Not tripped." and no warning about sends that never came back.

fields.label: The sending key's name in Resend (RESEND_SENDING_KEY_NAME)

steps.title: See the breaker trip, and the alert reach your phone
steps.body:
Both gate launch. The breaker's alert goes out through Healthchecks and ntfy, never through Resend, so it still reaches you when mail is the thing that failed.
1. Run the rehearsal test, with a stubbed Resend and never the real key. It must pass, in particular "trips at once, deletes the sending key, alerts without Resend".
2. Run `bin/nff alert test --production`. It sends the same down push and up push the breaker sends. **Done when a down push, then an up push, reach your iPhone through ntfy.**
3. Read `bin/nff breaker status` and `bin/nff breaker reset` once, so the first real trip is not the first time you see them.

steps.title: Make the encryption key on your Mac
steps.body:
Backups are encrypted before they leave the site. Only your private key can open them. In Terminal on your Mac (this downloads `age` with Homebrew):
```
brew install age
mkdir -p ~/Documents/nff-keys && cd ~/Documents/nff-keys
age-keygen -o nff-backup-key.txt
chmod 600 nff-backup-key.txt
```
It prints `Public key: age1…`. Paste that public key below; it's safe to share. Then save the **whole file** `nff-backup-key.txt` in your password manager, and keep a second copy offline (a USB stick at the farm, or with Jim). The private key never goes on Netlify or into a repository. **If the private key is lost, every backup is unreadable.**

steps.title: Cloudflare R2: bucket and token
steps.body:
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open **Storage & databases → R2** and complete the checkout to add R2. It may ask for a card; at this size it stays free.
2. **Create bucket.** Name it like the B2 one, with location hint **Eastern North America (enam)** and the Standard storage class.
3. In the bucket's **Settings → Object Lock**, turn it on and add a lock rule: Compliance mode, 30 days. Nothing can delete or overwrite a copy before then, even with the token below.
4. In **Object Lifecycle Rules → Add rule**: one rule, with no prefix, that deletes objects 30 days after they were created. Backups are kept 30 days (D-189), which is also how long deleted details can remain in them.
5. On the R2 Overview page, under **Account Details**, choose **Manage** API Tokens, then **Create Account API token**. Choose **Object Read & Write**, limit it to the one bucket, and create. R2 has no write-only token, so this one can read; that is accepted (D-EXPORT): the lock rule from step 3 stops deletes and overwrites, and the age encryption makes a read worthless. Copy the **Access Key ID**, the **Secret Access Key** (shown once) and the **S3 endpoint**, which looks like `https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`.

steps.title: Put the Netlify token in the Keychain
steps.body:
`bin/nff` reads the token from your Mac's Keychain and from no env file. Run this, then paste the new token when it asks (it stays out of your shell history):
```
security add-generic-password -a nff -s nff-netlify-auth-token -U -w
```
Then check `bin/nff --production health` works, and revoke the old token in Netlify. Remove any `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN` line from your `.env.*` files; `bin/nff env check` fails while one is there. The `netlify` CLI keeps its own login, which the next step retires.

steps.title: Log the Netlify CLI out for good
steps.body:
The CLI's own login sits in a plain file, `~/Library/Preferences/netlify/config.json`, with the same full access as the token in your Keychain. `bin/nff` passes the Keychain token to every Netlify command, so the file is not needed.
1. Run `bin/nff --production health` once to confirm the Keychain token works.
2. Run `netlify logout`.
3. Run `ls ~/Library/Preferences/netlify/config.json`. It should say the file does not exist.

From here on, run any Netlify command as `bin/nff netlify ...`. It works after the logout. **Never run `netlify login`**; the yearly rotation changes the Keychain token only.

steps.title: Email yourself when a deploy fails
steps.body:
Open **Project configuration → Notifications → Deploy notifications → Add notification → Email notification**. Event: **Deploy failed**. Your address. Save. Add no HTTP POST and no success notice.

Netlify can't limit notifications to production, so a staging failure emails you too; a phone page for every staging failure would be noise. A small function that filters for production deploy failures and pages your phone is approved for after launch (it is on the after-launch list).

steps.body: The staging token is for **machines only**: the Staging jobs workflow and health checks. You never type it into a browser, and the old "Staging token" prompt is gone. steps.title: Check the branch rules on GitHub
steps.body:
The security lane applied these on 2026-10-18; you only confirm them. Open **Settings, Rules, Rulesets** in `north-foster-farm`. There should be two, both **Active**, both with an **empty Bypass list**:
1. **fast-forward only: next, staging, main**: linear history, no force push, no deletion.
2. **required checks: staging, main**: `lint-and-test`, `supply-chain` and `codeql`, each from GitHub Actions. `audit` joins when you answer the advisories decision.

`next` requires no check, so lanes keep landing work. There is no pull-request rule on `main`, on purpose: GitHub's merge button cannot fast-forward, and a pull-request rule would reject the fast-forward push. `bin/nff promote main` checks your `LGTM` on the pull request instead. Whether to make GitHub enforce that with a second account is a decision below (D-SEC-REVIEWER). The full account is `docs/security.md`.

**Note, 2026-10-24:** The 2026-10-22 decision on #283 replaced the check above. You create a `staging` ruleset (lint-and-test, supply-chain, codeql, build, record-shape), narrow the old combined ruleset 25361919 to `main`, then create the `main` ruleset (the same list with release-audit in place of record-shape) and delete 25361919. `e2e` stays out of both while the e2e pause stands. The line in #237 is the master.

steps.title: Turn on GitHub's free security features
steps.body:
Both repositories are public for good (decided 2026-10-18), so GitHub's free security features apply. They need owner rights. In **each** repository, open Settings, then Code security:
1. **Secret scanning**, with **push protection**. Both are off today.
2. **Private vulnerability reporting**, so an outsider writes to you and not to a public issue.
3. In `nff-dashboard` only: **Dependabot alerts** and **Dependabot security updates**. They are off there, which is why it showed no alerts while `npm audit` finds several.
4. Leave **CodeQL's default setup off** in both. A workflow scoped to `next`, `staging` and `main` does the scanning, and the default setup would scan every branch as well.

Done when each setting reads Enabled.

steps.title: Make the two production-audit checks
steps.body:
A daily workflow audits what is live for known vulnerabilities and pings a Healthchecks check: a plain ping when clean, a failure when not, which pages your phone through the account you already use. Make two checks, **Production audit** and **Dashboard production audit**, each with period **1 day** and grace **3 hours**, assigned to the ntfy integration. Then, in each repository, add the check's URL as an Actions secret named `PROD_AUDIT_PING_URL` (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions, New repository secret).

Nothing runs until the workflow reaches `main`: the site's at launch, the dashboard's when its PR #30 merges, so the checks show "new" until then. Each URL goes in the **NFF launch** folder; the rotation log has its seed line.

steps.title: Make the dev@ address in Fastmail (blocking)

**Blocking launch gate:** deploy-failed, alert and rotation emails all go to this address, so the launch does not start without it and without the test two steps down.

In Fastmail, add the address **dev@northfosterfarm.com** (an alias on your own mailbox is enough). It receives incident steps, maintenance notices, rotation reminders and security alerts, kept apart from `FARM_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL`, which carries the farm's notices. The site reads it as `DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL`, set per environment; a later step has you put it in Netlify and the env files. A plain test message from your own mail proves the alias only; the real test follows the setting.

steps.title: Set DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL in Netlify
steps.body:
After the dev@ address works, set it on both contexts. It is an address, not a secret, so a plain variable is right. In the project folder:
```
netlify env:set DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL dev@northfosterfarm.com --context production --json
netlify env:set DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL dev+staging@northfosterfarm.com --context branch:staging --json
```
Then add `DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL=dev+staging@northfosterfarm.com` to your `.env.staging` and `DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL=dev@northfosterfarm.com` to your `.env.production` too, so `bin/nff env check` finds no difference. Use `--context`: `--scope` fails without saying so. Incident steps, rotation reminders and security alerts go to this address from the next deploy.

steps.title: Set the three notification addresses, and remove ADMIN_EMAILS
steps.body:
`ADMIN_EMAILS` is gone. Its uses split three ways, and each address is required in production and staging:
- `FARM_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL` = sales@northfosterfarm.com: the farm's notice of each new order, contact-form messages, the 8:00 morning report and the 18:00 tomorrow email. No alert goes there.
- `DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL` = dev@northfosterfarm.com: every alert, the maintenance flip notices, the session-end notice, the rotation reminder and the maintenance bypass's admin. Jim no longer hears the flips. An unset value fails the production build.
- `ESCALATED_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL` = office@northfosterfarm.com: one message only, when "orders not recorded" has gone unacknowledged for an hour, and again every hour while the alert stays open. Jim gets nothing else.

The guide's env builder writes all three. Staging uses plus-addresses of dev@ for all three (`dev+staging@`, `dev+staging-farm@`, `dev+staging-escalated@`): Fastmail delivers each to dev@, and the tag in the address tells you which one it was, so no staging mail reaches sales@ or office@. `env check` does not enforce this, since it only compares what each context holds. Check the `.env.production` and `.env.staging` you downloaded, then **delete the `ADMIN_EMAILS` line from both files and from Netlify** (the build and `env check` both fail while it exists anywhere; `env check` prints the unset command for a stray one on Netlify and never deletes). The two commands below do it. Then `bin/nff env push` and `env check`, as for the rest.

Check that it arrives in dev@ (look in spam too) and tell Claude. Repeat on production after the production value is set and deployed.

steps.title: Send the staging and production values to Netlify
steps.body:
In the project folder, in this order:
```
bin/nff env push --staging
bin/nff env check --staging
netlify env:unset STAGING_TOKEN --context production
bin/nff env push --production
bin/nff env check --production
```
Then ask Claude to deploy each context, staging and production.
- **Push a context before its sample reaches a build there.** Every staging and production build first checks that each key its committed sample lists is set (`check:env`), so a sample that lands before its push fails that context's next build. Staging failed this way until the optional keys were marked (the staging review item has the lists).
- **Production's first build fails the same check until production has been env pushed.** Run `bin/nff env push --production` and `bin/nff env check --production` before the release deploy, or the deploy fails and the old site stays up.
- `push` sets each key the sample lists, marks secrets as secret, skips local-only keys and never deletes anything. If it refuses because a secret is a plain variable on Netlify, mark that key secret in the Netlify UI, or run the `env:unset` commands it prints, then push again.
- `check` lists, by name only, anything that still differs. The `env:unset` lines it prints are yours to run; push never deletes.

Production's values match what it has today, so nothing changes for the live site.

A push then offers **Deploy now?** and posts the context's build hook; add `--allow-deploy` to skip the question. The Netlify calls in the push have never run live, so the first staging push is the rehearsal: if it stops, tell Claude what it printed (it prints names, never values).

**Then, in the same sitting, for the staging token:** put the new value in GitHub (**Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → STAGING_TOKEN → Update**), and ask Claude to rebuild staging. Until all three match, the staging jobs workflow fails.

steps.title: Where each value lives
steps.body:
The **NFF launch** folder in your password manager is the master copy of every value, and the only one you can read back. Netlify holds the values the site needs and the env files hold your working copies; none of those replaces the master.
- **Square, PayPal, Axiom, Healthchecks:** Netlify (production and staging contexts), your env files, the master copy.
- **Netlify token:** your Mac's Keychain and the master copy only; in no env file.
- **Staging keys:** `STAGING_TOKEN`, `E2E_STAGING_TOKEN` and the access gate's `GATE_RESEND_KEY`, `GATE_MAIL_FROM` and `GATE_TOOLBAR_EMAIL` on staging only. Never on production.
- **Resend:** production only; no staging team, key, audience or webhook. `RESEND_READ_KEY` and the old inbound secret go after launch day's live checks.
- **R2 backup token (`BACKUP_R2_*`):** Netlify production and the master copy.
- **Backup encryption key (age):** the private key lives on your Mac in `~/Documents/nff-keys` and never on Netlify. Backed up in the master copy, plus a second copy offline (a USB stick at the farm, or with Jim). Only the public key is on Netlify.
- **Backup check ping URL:** Netlify production, the master copy.
- **ntfy topic:** works like a password. Your iPhone, Healthchecks, the master copy.
- **`DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL`:** configuration, not a secret. Netlify per environment and the env files.
- **`MAINTENANCE_SECRET`:** Netlify (a secret value) and the env files, a different one per context, and the master copy. Without it only the command line flips the switch.

Until #251 is done, previews and local development still hold some shared values (step env-contexts). Delete this note when they don't.

steps.title: Retire the old shared credentials
steps.body:
Once staging runs on its new values:
- **Square:** delete the old shared sandbox webhook subscription. Keep the old app only if production uses it.
- **PayPal:** delete the old shared sandbox app.
- **Axiom and Healthchecks:** delete the token and checks staging used to share.
- **Resend:** delete the keys previews and staging used to share, but **not** production's `RESEND_READ_KEY` or its key at Resend. The live site reads it until launch day's live checks pass (step pw-p9); the launch is fixed forward, with no week's hold.
- **Your old Netlify token:** revoke it at Applications → Personal access tokens, once every env file, yours and the lanes', holds the new one.
- **Production's context:** delete `STAGING_TOKEN`, the gate's names and the retired `STAGING_REVIEWER_TOKEN` if any exists, even empty. Production fails its build and `bin/nff env check` while it holds one (b60a03b).

steps.title: Rehearse maintenance mode on staging
steps.body:
This is the safety net that replaces rolling back. With it on, nobody can order, pay, sign in or change an account, and every page shows one message. Rehearse it on staging with Claude before the release. Set staging's secret first ("Set the maintenance secret" above); without it only the commands work, not the phone links.
1. Turn staging's switch **on**: `bin/nff --staging maintenance on`. The notice goes to staging's outbox (Claude reads it there), not to a real inbox.
2. Open `/api/maintenance` on staging: it says maintenance is on. Open the order page and an account page. Each shows exactly the message below, and you can't order from either.
3. Open the order page in a tab *before* you flip the switch, then flip it and, in that tab, try to check out, edit an order and cancel one. Each shows the message and nothing goes through.
4. Claude runs the cases a page can't show: an open tab, a payment made just before the flip (it still finishes its order), a Square webhook that arrives while it is on (accepted), the flip notices and the phone links.
5. **Venmo, by hand:** start a sandbox Venmo payment, leave PayPal's window open, turn maintenance on, then approve. The capture still finishes, because the money has moved.
6. **On your phone:** run `bin/nff --staging maintenance links`. It prints an ON and an OFF link. Open the ON link: it shows a confirm page and flips nothing until you tap its button (so a link preview can't flip it). Tap, check the order page, then use the OFF link.
7. Turn it **off** with `bin/nff --staging maintenance off` if it is still on. A signed-in tab carries on, still signed in.

Tell Claude when it passes.

steps.title: Prove a republished deploy keeps its old env (staging)
steps.body:
The rollback runbook assumes that republishing an old deploy runs no build and serves the env values it was built with. Nobody has proved it. This test does, on staging, and it settles the first item in `docs/rollback.md` under *Not verified*. It needs Netlify access, so you run it or allow Claude to.
1. Set a harmless staging value, for example `SNAPSHOT_TEST` to `one`, and build a deploy.
2. Change it to `two`.
3. Republish the older deploy with `restoreSiteDeploy`. That runs no build.
4. Check which value its functions see, and whether auto publishing is now locked.
5. Redeploy (a new build) and check that `two` shows. That is the other half: a **redeploy** uses today's values, a **republish** uses the old ones.
6. Delete the test value.

Claude records the result on #267 and in the runbook. Until it is recorded, the rule stands: never publish a deploy built before a key change. Before launch if it fits; in any case before the second production release.

**Note, 2026-10-24:** The env-snapshot test is also scheduled with the one-tap rollback (#376), where it is required before the second release. You may do it after launch.

steps.title: Prove production's maintenance switch
steps.body:
Before any real-money check, test the switch once on production, so you know it works the moment you need it. It is also how you stop orders while a problem is fixed: the launch is fixed forward, with no rollback.
1. Turn it **on**: `bin/nff --production maintenance on`. dev@ gets an email, for real.
2. Open `/api/maintenance`: it says maintenance is on. In a private window, open the order page and an account page. Both show exactly the message below. Health still answers.
3. Turn it **off**: `bin/nff --production maintenance off`. Another email. Reload the order page and confirm it works again.
4. Keep the phone links: run `bin/nff --production maintenance links` and save the ON and OFF links on your phone. Whoever holds a link can flip the switch; `bin/nff --production maintenance rotate` kills every link handed out so far.

Don't start the payment checks until the order page works again.

1. In Firefox, open the order page with developer tools. Block requests to `web.squarecdn.com` (Network tab: right-click a request to it, then Block URL), then reload. A "payment unavailable" alert should reach your phone within a minute. Check that it does.
2. With Square still blocked, order $1 and pay by Venmo: scan the code with your phone and pay in the real Venmo app.
3. Unblock `web.squarecdn.com`.
4. Refund the $1 with `bin/nff --production orders refund <id>`. The id is on the success card. Check the order record, Square's copy and both webhooks agree.
5. In Square's dashboard, open the refund and check it shows **Completed**, not Pending. Sandbox left Venmo refunds pending (#164 item 1), so production is the first place this shows.

steps.title: Square: does the old token die on Replace, and does it expire?

steps.title: Restore from backups on a schedule, every path proven automatically
steps.body: `docs/backup.md` has only a one-off manual rehearsal. Your rule: restore regularly, and prove every restoration path works, automatically. Monthly, and once in each rotation window, a run fetches a recent backup, decrypts it, restores into scratch stores, compares counts and clears them. The paths: the online private key; the **offline copy** (the agents propose how a test can use an offline key without bringing it online, or a short manual step with the rest automated); production and staging backups; and `restore-db.mjs` for the dashboard's Supabase if it is in scope. A failure alerts you through healthchecks.io and each run appends to the rehearsal record. Pick the offline-key option when the proposal arrives.

steps.title: Dec 1 to Jan 1: rotate the Netlify token and the yearly secrets
steps.body:
Follow `docs/secrets.md`. Rotate every secret in the window, Dec 1 to Jan 1. The Netlify and Axiom tokens expire Jan 31, a month later, so a slip costs nothing. A reminder email arrives on Dec 1 with what is due, and weekly after that until the rotation log shows it done.

**Switch maintenance mode on first, for the Square token, and do it in a quiet hour inside the window.** Square gives the old token no grace, so checkout fails between pressing Replace and the new deploy going live. Run `bin/nff --production maintenance on`, replace the token, set it on Netlify, deploy, check a payment, then run `bin/nff --production maintenance off`. Customers see the maintenance message instead of a failed payment. The other secrets rotate without downtime and need no maintenance mode.

**Keep each old credential 31 days after the new one is live** (or until its own Jan 31 expiry, whichever is first), then revoke it, and log both dates in `docs/rotation-log.md` (the second line has reason `revoked`). Exceptions: the staging tokens and the maintenance secret are swapped at once, and a leak revokes at once. The age key's old private key (both copies) is kept the same 31 days so the 30-day backup window stays readable, then destroyed.

steps.title: Swapping the Square webhook key, and removing the old
steps.body:
Once the site accepts two webhook keys (the checkout lane's build), a swap has no gap: set the old value as `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY_PREVIOUS`, the new one as `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY`, deploy, and check a delivery verifies.

**Then, 31 days later, remove `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY_PREVIOUS` and deploy again.** The swap is safe only if the old key is gone afterward. On a leak, skip the overlap and remove the old key at once. Steps: [docs/secrets.md](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/blob/next/docs/secrets.md).

revisions.summary: Check the home page map on both. Switch to the **Delivery** layer and try the floating **Enter your ZIP** field; switch to **Places**; then check the map on About. Note: Foster's last market is **Oct 25**. After that, the home band lists no markets, which is expected.

revisions.changed: Your 10/17 review of the map, as two design reviews (A the places list and cards, B the area right of the map). Mock-ups only; nothing is built.
revisions.summary:
Two design reviews, each made twice without either pass seeing the other, then merged. **Nothing is built. Every word is a draft. Build waits for your yes.** The mock-ups below are 1280 and 1500 wide, with the phone (390) noted under each area. Open them on a laptop.

## A. The places list and the cards

You said the list "seems to have no real design language at all." What the passes agreed on:
- The card leaves the map and opens in its row in the list, one open at a time. The map keeps only pins, the town outline and the tint, so no card hides another pin (today the farm's card covers the drop site's pin).
- One card, one order, for the farm, the drop site, markets and pop-ups: when, where, directions, links (only where there are any), then the shop button (the farm and the drop site only). A card omits a part and never reorders one. The kind line and the repeated name go, and so does the tiny close button; tapping the row closes it.
- Chosen means lighter, never darker: the row gets a pale wash, a 3px left bar and a filled pin glyph; the pin turns a brighter blue and is drawn last; the town gets the blue outline.
- Hovering a row lifts its pin and hovering a pin lights its row. The list scrolls inside its column.
- Keyboard and screen readers: rows are buttons; Enter or Space opens, Escape closes and returns to the row.

**Phone (390):** the list sits right under the map, and a pin tap opens its row there, scrolling it into view only if needed. No sheet over the map: at 358 by 380 a sheet would cover half of it. At 390 by 844 the map and the first rows share one screen.

Where the two passes differed, I chose: phone row, not a sheet; a pin glyph in a small circle on each row; the town on the second line, then the day ("Foster; North Scituate · Saturdays"); 36px direction chips; small labels (When, Where, Directions, More); a violet-leaning blue tint for towns.

**Questions A1 to A4.**
- **A1. The card opens in the list, not on the map.** This departs from "opens its card" if you pictured it on the map. *Recommend yes* (nothing hidden, one design, works on a phone). If no: the floating card, restyled to the same template and kept clear of other pins.
- **A2. A small pin glyph in a circle on every row.** *Recommend keep.* It points to the pin and sorts nothing, so it is not a swatch. If it reads as one to you, drop it; the wash and the bar still tie the row to its pin.
- **A3. The tint for towns with a pin is violet-leaning blue (#e4e6f4), not pure blue.** *Recommend yes*: a plain pale blue reads as a lake beside the water.
- **A4. Row wording: the town, then the day.** *Recommend as drafted.*

## B. The area right of the map, on both tabs

You called the Delivery key the one that "makes me scratch my head," with "so much empty space below it," and asked for the column 35 to 50% narrower with the map nearer the center. What the passes agreed on:
- A column stays beside the map on both tabs, the same width and top edge, so switching tabs moves nothing. It starts level with the top of the map, not the toggle (today it sits about 60px high, which is half of why it looks adrift).
- The key is a bordered card with the map's border and radius, so the two read as a pair. The Places list sits in the same card. The card is only as tall as its content; the space below reads as margin beside a map, not a hole.
- Two labeled groups in the key, since it has two independent parts: the shading (price) and the icons (what we deliver). Your wording in the rows is unchanged.
- The toggle is alone above the map; the zoom buttons sit on the map, top right, stacked. No result card, no legend on the map, and the legend stays on Delivery only.

**Phone (390):** under 992px the card goes under the map. The key becomes two side-by-side groups about 110px tall; the ZIP field and zoom stay on the map; the tag and the key fit one screen.

Where the passes differed, I chose: a 300px column (not 288px); the map capped at 608px so the whole block fits a 768px laptop window; the heading stays centered; the key heads "Shading" and "Icons"; not sticky.

**Questions B1 to B4.**
- **B1. The column is 300px, which is 32% narrower than today's 442 at 1280, not 35%.** *Recommend yes.* At 288px (35%) the longest name, "The Village Family Fitness," wraps. One value to change if you want the number. **The decision that matters most:** is a column about 300px wide, with the map and the column centered, the "narrower and more central" you meant?
- **B2. The key's two heads: "Shading" and "Icons."** *Recommend as drafted.* Alternative: "Delivery price" and "What we deliver."
- **B3. Zoom buttons top right of the map, stacked.** *Recommend yes.*
- **B4. No empty-space fix beyond the card and the narrowing.** *Recommend yes*: filling the column would mean adding the prose you cut.

## A separate small bug: the Village card's "Website"

On the Village Family Fitness pop-up card, "Website" goes to the venue's Instagram page: `data/events.json` holds an Instagram URL as `href`, and the template labels any `href` "Website." Your rule is no Instagram on a pop-up card. *Recommend:* remove the link for this event now (the mock-ups show the card without it), add an `href` only when the venue has a real website, and never show an instagram.com `href` on a pop-up. Needs nothing from you unless you know the venue's website.

**To approve:** a yes or a change on A1 to A4 and B1 to B4.

A Tour of Our New Ordering System
October 18, 2026

**Ordering from the farm online has been open for a few weeks now.** This summer was the first we sold our chicken, and we're grateful to everyone who tried it. Now you can keep buying from us after the market season ends. Here's a tour of how it works.

Ordering
The order page has eggs by the dozen, whole chickens, cuts, and sausage. What's in stock changes as we go, and the page always shows what's available now. Choose what you'd like, say how you want to get it, and pay on the page. We email you to confirm your order.

There are three ways to get it:

Delivery
- We deliver every week on Thursday
- Order by noon on Wednesday
- As affordable as possible: $40 minimum, $5 fee
- Check your ZIP code

On-farm pickup
- Pick a day and a time when you order, 9 AM to 1 PM or 1 to 5 PM
- No fee, no minimum

Drop site
- Every Saturday morning in Scituate, 10:00 to 11:00 AM
- Pick up your order for free

Your account
You don't need an account to order. If you'd like one, there's no password: type the email you order with on the sign-in page and we'll send you a link that signs you in. Signed in, you can see past orders and receipts, change or cancel an order in progress, and keep a delivery address on file.

Farm news
News like this goes only to people who ask for it. You can sign up any time, or tick the email box when you place an order.

After market season
Our last market of the season is the Foster Farmers Market on October 25. After that, ordering online is the way to buy from us. Our hens, although slowing down, will keep laying all year round.

This is the first version of our online ordering system, and we want to hear how it works for you. Get in touch if you run into any problems.

— James and Jim

revisions.summary: Decided. Order records are kept indefinitely for historical reporting. Personal details on an order are removed after seven years; the order keeps the date, line items, prices, totals, channel, drop site, town and ZIP, and loses the name, emails, phone and street address. A customer can delete their personal details at any time; their orders stay, re-pointed to a deleted-household record (Null Object pattern), and deletion is final (a returning customer starts a new household, with no restore or re-link). Data export (download everything NFF holds) is planned after deletion ships, not before. Quiet accounts are never deleted automatically; after one year without interaction the household is unsubscribed from marketing mail and sent one transactional notice about how to delete if they'd like to. Signing in, an action while signed in, a badge-scanned market sale, or a click on a link in an email resets the one-year clock; an unsubscribe click or a visit only to opt out, change settings or delete does not. Email open tracking stays off permanently in Resend and every template; click and conversion tracking are fine. Nothing open in retention itself; the #189 spec can proceed. Data export (step two) needs its own spec later.

reviews.title: Where a full security scan report goes

revisions.summary:
On a public repository, workflow logs and uploaded files can be read by anyone, so neither may hold a finding. The planned ZAP scans (a passive baseline on production, an active one on staging through the gate's machine credential) will write only a pass or fail count to the log. The full report has to go somewhere private. Two choices:
- **Encrypted to your age key, in the private R2 bucket.** The runner encrypts before upload, as the backups do. Nothing readable leaves the runner, and the key that reads it stays on your Mac.
- **Mailed to `DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL`.** Simpler, but findings sit in a mailbox.

The same applies to any later audit's findings. Neither is built, and the scans are not yet either.
revisions.recommendation: The encrypted file in R2. Say "mail" if you would rather have it in your inbox.

- *Recommend the copy lane's clearer set* ([5877467523](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/165#issuecomment-5877467523)): "Download order history (CSV)" and "Download payments and refunds (CSV)" (a refund isn't a receipt); headers "Pickup or delivery", "Pickup or delivery date", "Type" and "Paid by"; "PayPal transaction" before a Venmo id; the second file named `north-foster-farm-payments-{date}.csv`.
- Scheduled pickup (#309) changes one cell: a pickup at the drop site, a market or a pop-up reads "Scheduled pickup, {place}" (draft). #312 carries it.

**3. Retention and quiet accounts** ([#189](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/189#issuecomment-6333143727)). The rules are on `next` and staging. Five calls, none urgent, since no notice can go before about September 2027:
- **a. Forget quiet accounts, or keep them?** Your 10/22 comment says forgotten; D-189 and the privacy page say kept until the customer closes it. *Recommend keep (D-189).*
- **b. A placed order counts as interaction,** guest orders included. *Recommend yes.*
- **c. Email clicks as interaction.** Resend's click tracking would route sign-in links through its redirect. *Recommend no click tracking.* If you want clicks on farm news, count them later through our own redirect.
- **d. Approve the privacy sentence and the one-time notice** ([6333314214](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/189#issuecomment-6333314214); held as 62f06ce). *Recommend approve as written.*
- **e. Delivery pass emails** ([#301](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/301)). *Recommend:* a single-use pass drops its email once it is used, expires or is revoked; a standing pass goes with its customer when the customer is deleted.

**4. The map's sand and town lines** ([#214](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/214#issuecomment-6332195764)). The white town lines on the $8 sand are faint (1.43:1). Crisper lines need a darker sand, which narrows its step from the $5 green.
- *Recommend a darker sand,* since you asked twice for the lines to read clearly, keeping a visible step to the green. The map lane posts before and after at 390 and 1280.
- The Places section names ("Pickup", "Markets and pop-ups") need no answer: scheduled pickup (#314) replaces both with one list.

**5. The cart at mid sizes** ([#274](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/274#issuecomment-6330804018)). The workshop shows the floating pane at 768, 1024 and phone landscape: at 768 and 1024 the list column shows one and a half lines, a pane floats even when empty, and the collapsed row leaves a wide gap. You haven't picked a direction.
- *Recommend:* no floating pane with nothing in the cart, at any width; the phone's one-column pane (Items and Total) up to 1023 px, phone landscape included; from 1024 the right-column cart that xl uses, sticky beside the catalog. The checkout lane mocks these at 768, 1024 and 844 by 390 before building.

**6. "cancelled" or "canceled"** ([#159](https://github.com/north-foster-farm/north-foster-farm/issues/159)). About 30 places in customer copy use the British spelling; the stored status key `cancelled` stays either way.
- *Recommend one sweep to "canceled"* in the copy, to match the site's American English.

groups.title: Site
groups.about: Which deploy this is, and the address links in emails point at. Set per Netlify deploy context.

groups.title: Square
groups.about: Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Cash App Pay. Log in at developer.squareup.com/apps. Each environment has its own application: Credentials holds the IDs and token, Webhooks > Subscriptions the signature key. Development uses the fake driver.

groups.title: PayPal (Venmo)
groups.about: Venmo through PayPal. Log in at developer.paypal.com/dashboard, Apps & Credentials (Sandbox or Live toggle). Each environment has its own app; the webhook ID is listed under the app's webhooks. Development uses the fake driver.

groups.title: Mail
groups.about: How email leaves the site: resend in production, the outbox on staging (read it in the browser), files on disk in development.

groups.title: Resend
groups.about: Sends transactional email and keeps the farm-news contacts. Log in at resend.com/login. Keys are made at resend.com/api-keys and shown once; webhooks at resend.com/webhooks. Production and staging are separate teams, if staging has one at all. Simulated in development.

groups.title: Logs and alerts
groups.about: Axiom keeps the log lines (app.axiom.co, Settings > API tokens, ingest-only tokens, one dataset per environment). Healthchecks pages James's phone (healthchecks.io; each check's ping URL is on its page). Not used in development.

groups.title: Backups
groups.about: The nightly encrypted export, to two places: Backblaze B2 (secure.backblaze.com, Application Keys) and Cloudflare R2 (dash.cloudflare.com, R2 > Manage API tokens). Encrypted to an age public key; the private key never leaves James's password manager. Names are proposed until the export is built.

groups.title: Staging tools
groups.about: Guards the staging back office (/api/staging) and lets the browser tests read the outbox. Also stored as the GitHub Actions secret STAGING_TOKEN.

groups.title: Local tools
groups.about: Read only by bin/nff and the browser tests on James's Mac. Never set on Netlify. The Netlify token is a personal access token (app.netlify.com/user/applications), expiring each Jan 1.

vars.name: SITE_CONTEXT
vars.comment: Which deploy this is. Picks the Blobs store names (production uses the bare names) and turns staging behaviour on or off. bin/nff sets it from its flag.

vars.name: SITE_URL
vars.comment: The site's own address. Links in emails start with it, and Square signs its webhooks against it.

vars.name: ACCOUNTS_ENABLED
vars.comment: true puts account links (sign in, your orders) in emails.

vars.name: MAINTENANCE_SECRET
vars.comment: Signs the phone links that flip maintenance mode. A different value per context.

vars.name: SQUARE_ENV
vars.comment: Which Square to talk to: production, sandbox, or fake (no network, development and tests).

vars.name: SQUARE_APPLICATION_ID
vars.comment: The application ID. Public: the order page's payment form uses it.

vars.name: SQUARE_LOCATION_ID
vars.comment: The Square location the website's sales belong to.

vars.name: SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN
vars.comment: The application's access token (Credentials > Show). Replacing it switches the old one off at once.

vars.name: SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY
vars.comment: Checks that webhook calls really come from Square (Webhooks > Subscriptions > the subscription > Signature Key).

vars.name: PAYPAL_ENV
vars.comment: Which PayPal to talk to: live, sandbox, or fake (development and tests).

vars.name: PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID
vars.comment: The app's Client ID. Public: the Venmo button uses it.

vars.name: PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET
vars.comment: The app's Secret.

vars.name: PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID
vars.comment: The webhook's ID, which PayPal needs to check each webhook call. Shown in the app's webhook list.

vars.name: VENMO_HIDDEN
vars.comment: 1 shows Venmo as Coming soon, except to a browser that opened the order page with ?venmo. Empty or 0 shows it. Production leaves it empty; setting it to 1 is the kill switch.

vars.name: MAIL_DRIVER
vars.comment: resend sends for real; outbox keeps mail in the site's store to read in the browser; file writes each email to MAIL_OUT.

vars.name: MAIL_OUT
vars.comment: The folder the file driver writes to.

vars.name: MAIL_FROM
vars.comment: The sender name and address.

vars.name: MAIL_REPLY_TO
vars.comment: Where customers' replies go.

vars.name: FARM_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL
vars.comment: The farm's address: each new order, the contact form, the 8:00 morning report and the 18:00 tomorrow email. No alerts. Not a secret.

vars.name: DEV_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL
vars.comment: The developer's address: every alert, the maintenance flip and session-end notices, and the rotation reminder. Not a secret.

vars.name: ESCALATED_NOTIFICATIONS_EMAIL
vars.comment: Jim's address: one plain-language message, when "orders not recorded" stays unacknowledged. Nothing else. Not a secret.

vars.name: RESEND_API_KEY
vars.comment: The sending key: Sending access, limited to the mail domain.

vars.name: RESEND_AUDIENCE_ID
vars.comment: The farm-news contact list (Resend now calls it a segment).

vars.name: RESEND_AUDIENCE_KEY
vars.comment: A full-access key for the nightly contact sync.

vars.name: RESEND_SENDING_KEY_NAME
vars.comment: The sending key's name in Resend, which the send breaker uses to find the key. Not a secret.

vars.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
vars.comment: Checks that webhook calls (unsubscribes) really come from Resend: the webhook's Signing Secret.

vars.name: AXIOM_TOKEN
vars.comment: Ingest-only token for this environment's dataset; expires Jan 1.

vars.name: AXIOM_DATASET
vars.comment: The dataset log lines go to.

vars.name: HEALTHCHECKS_JOBS_URL
vars.comment: Ping URL of the jobs heartbeat check.

vars.name: HEALTHCHECKS_ALERT_URL
vars.comment: Ping URL of the alerts check; alerts post to its /fail.

vars.name: HEALTHCHECKS_BACKUP_URL
vars.comment: Ping URL of the Backup check; a missed night trips it.

vars.name: BACKUP_AGE_RECIPIENT
vars.comment: The age public key backups are encrypted to (age1...).

vars.name: BACKUP_B2_ENDPOINT
vars.comment: Backblaze's S3 endpoint for the bucket.

vars.name: BACKUP_B2_BUCKET
vars.comment: The Backblaze bucket.

vars.name: BACKUP_B2_KEY_ID
vars.comment: The application key's keyID.

vars.name: BACKUP_B2_APPLICATION_KEY
vars.comment: The application key itself (shown once).

vars.name: BACKUP_R2_ENDPOINT
vars.comment: Cloudflare R2's S3 endpoint (https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com).

vars.name: BACKUP_R2_BUCKET
vars.comment: The R2 bucket.

vars.name: BACKUP_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID
vars.comment: The R2 token's Access Key ID.

vars.name: BACKUP_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
vars.comment: The R2 token's Secret Access Key (shown once).

vars.name: STAGING_TOKEN
vars.comment: A long random value. Also the GitHub Actions secret of the same name.

vars.name: E2E_STAGING_TOKEN
vars.comment: The end-to-end suite's own token. Also the GitHub Actions secret of the same name, and in .env.e2e-staging.

vars.name: GATE_RESEND_KEY
vars.comment: The access gate's own Resend sending key, made for staging and never production's. Sends the sign-in link and nothing else. Rotated Dec 1 to Jan 1.

vars.name: GATE_MAIL_FROM
vars.comment: The sender of the sign-in link, on a verified domain. Public: not a secret.

vars.name: GATE_TOOLBAR_EMAIL
vars.comment: The one address whose gate session opens the staging toolbar (yours). Public: not a secret.

vars.name: PICKUP_SCHEDULE_HOOK
vars.comment: A staging build hook. bin/nff schedule set starts a deploy with it after setting the schedule.

vars.name: NETLIFY_SITE_ID
vars.comment: The Project ID, so bin/nff can reach this site's records.
